worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-3$ and $\sigma =10.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.7<X<16.3) & =P(\frac{-0.7-(-3)}{10}<Z<\frac{16.3-(-3)}{10}) \\  & =P(0.23<Z<1.93).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/0f8530cb0d0742970ede7aac334b627e68619a7b39f6e553774fe5bdece99d4b.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.23<Z<1.93) & =P(Z<1.93)-P(Z\le 0.23) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.93)-P(Z\le 0.23) \\  & =Φ(1.93)-Φ(0.23).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.93) & =0.9732 \\ Φ(0.23) & =0.5910\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.23<Z<1.93) & =Φ(1.93)-Φ(0.23) \\  & =0.9732-0.5910 \\  & =0.3822.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-0.7<X<16.3)=0.3822.
$$

P(0.23<Z<1.93)=P(Z<1.93)−P(Z≤0.23)=P(Z≤1.93)−P(Z≤0.23)=Φ(1.93)−Φ(0.23).
